title: Smooth/regular-immersion interchange and section cancellation
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, $n\geq1$, and $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$. Work with separated finite-type compactifiable maps of Noetherian schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-asd-compactifiable]. Use ordinary small-etale derived categories and compact-support right adjoints [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], [def-amb-etale-compact-support], [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. For a regular closed immersion $i$ of codimension $c$, put $i^?=i^!(c)[2c]$ and write $a_i:\Lambda\to i^?\Lambda$ for its supported Kummer class [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus]. For a smooth map $q$ of dimension $r$, put $q^?=q^!(-r)[-2r]$ and write $a_q:\Lambda\to q^?\Lambda$ for the shifted diagonal/DNC orientation [lem-per-noetherian-prime-power-smooth-duality]. Regular immersions and smooth maps mean [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. In formulas let $a_v\star a_u=u^?(a_v)\circ a_u$, using exceptional transitivity and the canonical twist identifications.

For a Cartesian square $Z'=Z\times_X X'$ with regular closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$, smooth $q:X'\to X$, and projections $j:Z'\hookrightarrow X'$, $q':Z'\to Z$, one has
$$a_q\star a_j=a_i\star a_{q'}.$$
For a smooth map $q:V\to S$ with a closed section $s:S\hookrightarrow V$, one has
$$a_q\star a_s=1_{\Lambda_S}.$$
These are equalities of the specified maps, including their Kummer signs, and hold over arbitrary Noetherian bases, not only bases smooth over a field.

source.place: Expose XVI, Lemmas 2.5.7 and 2.5.8 (the two identities), with the smooth orientation replaced by the diagonal/DNC normalization of lem-per-noetherian-prime-power-smooth-duality. Source proof uses a classical trace route; the replacement is justified by the diagonal/DNC coordinate normalization in Scholze Theorem 7.19 and the section-deformation comparison lem-trf-finite-ring-section-deformation. No classical trace theorem is taken as an input.

from.place: Proof Step 3: dimension-normalized Verdier duality, regular finite-torsion local model; pointwise purity and composition used to compare the normalized curve with the ambient regular scheme. Input: Smooth/regular-immersion interchange and section cancellation.
